cards.context: Anthony Gonzalez and Nicolas Fromageau's second album together (Gooom, 2003).
cards.headline: Compared to My Bloody Valentine before they'd ever heard them
cards.snippet: The comparisons started with the album itself: Dead Cities, Red Seas & Lost Ghosts drew what No Ripcord counted as 'a hundred or so comparisons to My Bloody Valentine.' The odd part is how late Gonzalez and Fromageau came to the band they were being compared to: 'Actually, we only started listening to MBV after our first record. We heard all these people saying how the music sounds similar, so we checked them out.' The two had played together since they were 15, formed M83 in Antibes in 1999 and named it after the galaxy Messier 83; this album was recorded at M83 Studio in Antibes.

cards.context: Track 3 on Dead Cities, Red Seas & Lost Ghosts; the album's lead single, released 23 June 2003.
cards.headline: The duo's last album, and a slow trip to America
cards.snippet: Dead Cities, Red Seas & Lost Ghosts is founding member Nicolas Fromageau's last album with M83 — he left after touring it, leaving Anthony Gonzalez the project's sole constant member. Released in Europe on 14 April 2003, it reached North America more than a year later, on 27 July 2004, in a pressing whose bonus disc carried the 'Run Into Flowers' video. Pitchfork scored the album 9.2 and later ranked it No. 22 on its list of the 50 Best Shoegaze Albums of All Time; by 2005 it had sold close to 25,000 copies in the United States. The cover art is Justine Kurland's photograph Snow Angels.

cards.context: Posted under the official video. A longer one, kept whole — the argument is the point.
cards.headline: Against pristine production
cards.snippet: I think more electronic artists need to hear this. The focus these days tends to be on making music as pristine sounding as possible, which isn't necessarily a bad thing, but it's not the most important thing. This entire album really feels like M83 just poured their emotions into these pieces and didnt worry about pitch-perfect mixes or marketability. Really think we need more of that in modern electronic music.

cards.context: The song returned to M83's setlists on the Fantasy tour, after more than a decade away.
cards.headline: Live on KEXP, twenty years on
cards.snippet: M83 brought the song back for the Fantasy tour after more than a decade away from it. This KEXP session was recorded on 2 October 2023, with Gonzalez fronting a five-piece band. One listener from that video: 'Hearing this live gave me a spiritual awakening.' — @theshield2207, 21 likes

cards.context: One of three remixes on the song's 2003 single.
cards.headline: Jackson's 'Midnight Fuck' remix, the remix that got him signed
cards.snippet: The album's lead single, released 23 June 2003, carried three remixes, and Jackson Fourgeaud's radical 7:32 rework of this song eclipsed the others: it landed at the peak of Michael Mayer's Fabric 13 mix, and the splash it created led to Jackson and His Computerband's signing with Warp Records.
